request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 40.8% (95% band 24.3% to 53.1%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.3; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.57, 95% band [+2.13, +2.68]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 19.5% (95% band 13.6% to 25.1%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 149999: +0.2; >= 150000: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.99, 95% band [-1.34, -0.45]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 13.0% (95% band 6.1% to 16.9%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1890: +0.16; >= 1891: 0 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.62, 95% band [-0.89, -0.25]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 3.7% (95% band 0.0% to 6.5%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.18, 95% band [-0.05, +0.51]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.9% (95% band 0.0% to 5.8%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.08, 95% band [-0.12, +0.24]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.2% to 7.5%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.12, 95% band [-0.03, +0.50]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.1% to 8.3%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.08, 95% band [-0.41, +0.03]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 4.2%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.02, 95% band [-0.14, +0.26]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 2.8%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.01, 95% band [-0.15, +0.05]).

Interactions: the model has 18 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 2.8% (95% band 1.4% to 6.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.38 (95% band +1.93 to +2.62) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.69 (95% band +1.84 to +2.97) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.02 (95% band -1.28 to -0.46) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.71 (95% band -1.37 to -0.17) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.8% (95% band 0.0% to 3.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.23 (95% band +0.98 to +2.57) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.60 (95% band +1.96 to +2.75) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.00 (95% band -0.05 to +0.80) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.37 (95% band -0.01 to +1.47) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.8% (95% band 0.8% to 3.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.37 (95% band +1.86 to +2.58) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +2.70 (95% band +2.07 to +2.91) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.69 (95% band -0.99 to -0.28) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.36 (95% band -0.84 to +0.09) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.0% to 2.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.94 (95% band -1.27 to -0.45) when `AGE` = 23, -1.11 (95% band -1.46 to -0.45) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.21 (95% band +0.00 to +0.61) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.03 (95% band -0.12 to +0.44) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.0% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.63 (95% band +2.15 to +2.80) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +2.36 (95% band +1.84 to +2.68) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,900.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,900: -0.06 (95% band -0.42 to +0.05) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.33 (95% band -0.81 to +0.09) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.0% to 2.7%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.91 (95% band -1.28 to -0.44) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, -1.07 (95% band -1.45 to -0.46) when `PAY_AMT3` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 18,100: +0.19 (95% band -0.04 to +0.53) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.02 (95% band -0.25 to +0.17) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.00 (95% band -1.35 to -0.40) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -0.98 (95% band -1.41 to -0.45) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.66 (95% band -0.90 to -0.15) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.64 (95% band -0.95 to -0.24) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.65 (95% band -0.91 to -0.24) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, -0.62 (95% band -0.98 to -0.25) when `PAY_AMT3` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 18,100: +0.06 (95% band -0.13 to +0.25) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.10 (95% band -0.14 to +0.24) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.2%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.68 (95% band +2.14 to +2.75) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +2.53 (95% band +2.13 to +2.69) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.00 (95% band -0.12 to +0.03) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.15 (95% band -0.27 to +0.03) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.95 (95% band -1.39 to -0.45) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -1.09 (95% band -1.41 to -0.45) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,900.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,900: -0.02 (95% band -0.46 to +0.17) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.16 (95% band -0.46 to +0.05) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.60 (95% band -1.07 to -0.25) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.64 (95% band -0.98 to -0.25) when `BILL_AMT2` = 196,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 196,000: +0.04 (95% band -0.18 to +0.34) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -0.00 (95% band -0.16 to +0.41) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
- 7 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 1.6%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by the applicant's most recent repayment status, PAY_0, which accounts for about 41% of the model's importance (with a wide plausible range of roughly 24% to 53%)."},{"id":2,"text":"Being behind on payments in the latest month raises the predicted risk of default sharply: a delay of two months or more adds about +2 on the log-odds scale, while paying in full lowers it slightly and a value of 1 (one month's delay) adds a smaller +0.3."},{"id":3,"text":"The size of the credit limit, LIMIT_BAL, is the second most important driver at about 20% importance; higher limits are associated with lower predicted risk, with a net effect of roughly -1.0 log-odds between the 5th and 95th percentile."},{"id":4,"text":"The amount paid in the latest month, PAY_AMT1, is the third driver at about 13% importance, with larger payments (above roughly 1,890 NT dollars) associated with lower predicted risk, a net change of about -0.6."},{"id":5,"text":"The effects of PAY_0 and LIMIT_BAL interact: the drop in risk from a higher credit limit is somewhat larger when the applicant is current on payments, although the uncertainty on this difference is wide, so the data do not settle its size precisely."},{"id":6,"text":"Age, earlier payment amounts, earlier bill amounts and education each carry little importance, and their effects are not resolved at this sample size, so the data do not show that they reliably move predicted default risk."},{"id":7,"text":"Several other pairwise interactions exist but each is small, so they are not needed to understand the model's main behaviour."}]}
